## OppNarrative 1 — F1 (Hormuz closure by June 9)

**Claim being opposed:** p=0.40→0.55 (Analyst) that Iran takes a NEW concrete action to fully close Hormuz before June 9.

**Best contrary evidence:** The strait is already effectively closed since March 2026; Rubio confirmed "large segments" mined June 2; IRGC mine-laying has been continuous; US drones shot down June 6. Every IRGC operation is continuation of a pre-existing campaign. The ambiguity rule excluding "continuation of pre-existing de facto closure" is doing enormous work. gCaptain notes NAVCENT and commercial AIS disagree on what "transiting" even means, making a "fully closed" determination genuinely ambiguous. Even the June 6 tanker attacks may fall under the "continuation" exclusion rather than constituting a new discrete action.

**What would prove the report wrong within 7 days:** Iran issues a formal, signed, publicly declared total-closure/exclusion order; OR NAVCENT issues a new advisory explicitly citing new discrete mine-laying event after June 2 with geographic coordinates.

**DA recommendation:** REDUCE p from 0.40 to 0.25.

**Judge ruling:** PARTIAL ACCEPT. DA's core argument — that June 6 tanker attacks are "continuation" under the ambiguity rule — is correct. DA's 0.25 is too aggressive a reduction; June 6 attacks are a genuine escalation in operational intensity. Judge adopts 0.35 (above DA's 0.25, well below Analyst's 0.55). DA's falsifier is correct and incorporated into the updated ambiguity rule.

## OppNarrative 2 — F3 and F5 (Hormuz transit volumes)

**Judge ruling:** ACCEPT for F5; N/A for F3 (already resolved NO). DA's arguments on transit volumes are empirically correct. F5 reduced to 0.15. F9 (new) set at 0.18 using same logic. DA's falsifier is correctly specified and incorporated into F9's indicators.

## OppNarrative 3 — F7 (Netanyahu coalition collapse by Oct 27)

**Claim being opposed:** p=0.82 (Analyst cold-start) that coalition loses majority before Oct 27.

**Best contrary evidence:** The 106-0 dissolution vote June 2 shows the coalition IS engineering a controlled dissolution — not a collapse. Netanyahu retains enough Knesset support to pass legislation when he chooses to; this paradoxically means he maintains functional working majority through the dissolution process. The distinction between "coalition loses majority in Knesset" (the YES condition) and "coalition prepares for elections" (current situation) is precisely the ambiguity the resolution criteria struggles with. Polls showing 49-51 seats are electoral projections, not current Knesset seat counts. UTJ members may still vote with coalition on procedural matters without formally being coalition members.

**What would prove the report wrong within 7 days:** A formal coalition confidence vote that fails; a Knesset vote where Netanyahu's government is defeated on a substantive non-dissolution motion; a formal declaration by a current coalition party that it is withdrawing support.

**DA recommendation:** INCREASE p from 0.35 to 0.45 only. Flag that YES condition (formal majority loss) may not be triggered by controlled dissolution.

**Judge ruling:** ACCEPT. DA's argument that controlled dissolution does not trigger the YES resolution criterion is correct. The 106-0 vote demonstrates functional working majority on non-confidence matters. Judge adopts 0.45 (DA's upper bound). Analyst's cold-start of 0.85 rejected. DA's falsifier is correctly specified and aligns with Judge's own resolution criteria reading.
